_doc: Mature-peer benchmarks for Damodaran young-company DCF (ADR-028). Each entry names a mature, scaled-up peer with established steady-state economics, used as the TARGET that the young company can plausibly reach. Target operating margin and sales-to-capital ratio come from the peer's last 3-5 year averages.
_source: Hand-curated using Damodaran's industry data + peer-company filings. Refresh annually.
_methodology_notes: Target op margin is the mature peer's last-3yr-average operating margin
Sales-to-capital ratio = (3yr-avg revenue) / (3yr-avg invested capital). Damodaran's published industry table provides defaults.
Peer selection priority: similar business model > similar end-market > similar size at maturity

Healthcare Information Tech.notes: Veeva is the canonical mature health-IT cloud platform. 25% steady-state op margin reflects scale economics; sales-to-capital 2.5 reflects capital-light SaaS. For genomics/AI-diagnostics tickers (TEM, NTRA), this is the aspirational endpoint.

Drugs (Biotechnology).notes: Vertex represents a successfully scaled rare-disease biotech. 30% steady-state op margin; lower sales-to-capital reflects R&D + manufacturing capital intensity.

Software (System & Application).notes: Adobe represents mature software-platform economics. 35% op margin from subscription scale + brand pricing.

Software (Internet).notes: Meta represents network-effect internet at scale. Lower sales-to-capital reflects data-center capex.

Information Services.notes: ServiceNow is the SaaS information-services benchmark. For INTA-class platforms, this is the target.

Computer Services.notes: Accenture-style services have lower margins than product SaaS but higher capital efficiency. For PATH-class automation/AI services.

Semiconductor.notes: TSMC represents mature fabless/foundry semis. High margins, capital-heavy (low sales-to-capital).

Retail (Online).notes: Amazon represents mature scale-economics online retail. Op margin understates because AWS pulls it up.

Retail (Apparel).notes: Nike represents mature apparel-brand economics. For aspirational DTC apparel ticker IVs.

Financial Services (Non-bank).notes: Visa represents the elite payments-network endpoint. Very high op margin from network moat; very high capital efficiency.

_fallback_default.notes: Fallback when industry isn't in the table. 15% op margin and 2.0 sales-to-capital are Damodaran's published US-market median. Will trigger data_gap; user should specify peer explicitly.
